title: From If/Else Rules to CNNs: Evolution of Natural Language Processing

cues.en: Instructor: Hello and welcome back to the course on deep natural language processing.
cues.zh: 講師：大家好，歡迎回到深度自然語言處理課程。

cues.en: And today we're talking about classical versus deep learning models.
cues.zh: 今天談傳統與深度學習模型。

cues.en: So let's have a look.
cues.zh: 來看看。

cues.en: As we discussed, we've got this diagram and on the left, we've got the natural language processing models overall.
cues.zh: 如先前所說，左邊是整體自然語言處理模型。

cues.en: And on the right, we have the deep learning models overall.
cues.zh: 右邊是整體深度學習模型。

cues.en: So, their overlap is the deep natural language processing.
cues.zh: 重疊就是深度自然語言處理。

cues.en: Those are the very advanced types of natural language processing models which use deep learning.
cues.zh: 也就是使用深度學習的進階 NLP 模型。

cues.en: And then finally at the bottom here, we've got the sequence-to-sequence models, which we'll be interested in at the end.
cues.zh: 最後底下是序列到序列，最後會著重這個。

cues.en: And so I thought that this tutorial would be fun if we had a look at a comparison between a couple.
cues.zh: 我想這堂比較幾個模型，會很有趣。

cues.en: So we'll look at a couple of examples from here.
cues.zh: 看看這裡的幾個例子。

cues.en: We'll look at an example from here.
cues.zh: 也看看這裡一個例子。

cues.en: And then finally we'll mention the sequence-to-sequence, just to kind of lay out the playing field so we know what we're dealing with and what types exist there
cues.zh: 最後提序列到序列，先了解全貌，知道有哪些類型、正在處理什麼，

cues.en: because we could definitely just jump into sequence-to-sequence and look at the most powerful things.
cues.zh: 因為確實可以直接跳進最強的序列到序列。

cues.en: But then it would still be a mystery.
cues.zh: 但那樣仍有謎團。

cues.en: What are natural language processing models?
cues.zh: 什麼是 NLP 模型？

cues.en: How they different to deep natural language processing models?
cues.zh: 和深度 NLP 差在哪？

cues.en: And how are they different to sequence-to-sequence?
cues.zh: 又與序列到序列有什麼不同？

cues.en: What are the applications? And so on.
cues.zh: 有哪些應用？等等。

cues.en: So let's have a look at a couple of examples.
cues.zh: 來看幾個例子。

cues.en: All right, some examples, we're gonna have our diagram on the right and we're gonna start going through these examples one by one.
cues.zh: 右邊保留圖，逐一介紹例子。

cues.en: So number one is the if/else rules and this is a way that we used to create chatbots
cues.zh: 第一個 if/else 規則，是以前建立聊天機器人

cues.en: back in the day.
cues.zh: 的方法。

cues.en: So if/else rules are located over here on our diagram in just the NLP part, and what they entail is a huge list
cues.zh: 在圖中這裡，只有 NLP 的區域，內容是龐大的

cues.en: of possible questions and answers to those questions.
cues.zh: 可能問題及對應答案清單。

cues.en: And so once somebody in the chat asks a question, or we can identify that part of the sentence is the question that we have prerecorded,
cues.zh: 有人在聊天裡問問題，或辨識出句子一部分符合預先記錄的問題，

cues.en: then we will give them the correct answer, the answer that is associated with that question.
cues.zh: 就給正確答案，也就是與該問題關聯的答案。

cues.en: But as you can imagine, such mechanical- such a mechanical approach to answering questions or chatting with people does not result
cues.zh: 但可以想像，這種機械式問答或聊天方式，產生的結果

cues.en: in anything humanlike, anything realistic.
cues.zh: 不像人、不真實。

cues.en: And it results in something like this, rather where you have questions and then you have the predetermined answers.
cues.zh: 比較像這樣，問題搭配預定答案。

cues.en: But people want something tailored to them, something specific, they're asking about something else, but doesn't fit into that list of questions and answers.
cues.zh: 但人們想要量身打造、具體的內容，問的又可能是清單沒有的其他東西。

cues.en: And it just very quickly becomes a mess.
cues.zh: 很快就變得混亂。

cues.en: But that's how we used to create chatbots.
cues.zh: 但以前就是這樣做聊天機器人。

cues.en: The next type, or the next natural language processing model we will look at,
cues.zh: 下一種類型，下一個 NLP 模型，

cues.en: is called an audio frequency components analysis.
cues.zh: 叫音訊頻率成分分析。

cues.en: And it's used for speech recognition and sits over here.
cues.zh: 用於語音辨識，位於這裡。

cues.en: So we are specifically looking- like we are purposefully looking at different examples.
cues.zh: 我們刻意看不同例子。

cues.en: So not just chatbots, we're looking at different applications.
cues.zh: 不只聊天機器人，還有不同應用。

cues.en: So you can see that NLP can be applied to speech recognition.
cues.zh: 可以看到 NLP 能用在語音辨識。

cues.en: And there used to be- or still are- algorithms that use non-deep learning methods for speech recognition.
cues.zh: 以前，甚至現在，仍有非深度學習的語音辨識演算法。

cues.en: And one of them is audio frequency components analysis.
cues.zh: 其中之一就是音訊頻率成分分析。

cues.en: So in essence what happens is we look at the sound wave of, somebody talking, some prerecorded or real time audio over human speech
cues.zh: 基本上，觀察人說話的聲波，預錄或即時的人類語音，

cues.en: and then we try to identify what wave forms exist in there.
cues.zh: 試著辨識裡面有哪些波形。

cues.en: So in a very kind of simple way of explaining it, let's have a look at, for example here we've got a four year transformation and we've got the
cues.zh: 用很簡單的方式說明，例如這裡有傅立葉轉換，還有，

cues.en: there's our frequency over there.
cues.zh: 這邊是頻率。

cues.en: So it's like one of these is going over there.
cues.zh: 像這其中一個延伸到那裡。

cues.en: Of course this is, this doesn't even look like human speech to be frank, but the concept stays.
cues.zh: 坦白說，這甚至不像人類語音，但概念相同。

cues.en: So, like, we look at what frequencies can it consists of, and then, we compare them to, like, the prerecorded frequencies.
cues.zh: 查看由哪些頻率構成，再與預錄頻率比較。

cues.en: So we know that, for instance, certain, certain combination of frequencies means this type of word or this type of word.
cues.zh: 例如知道某種頻率組合代表這類或那類詞。

cues.en: And it's not just about the frequencies, of course, it's it's much more complex than that.
cues.zh: 當然不只頻率，複雜得多。

cues.en: But this is a very general overview of what happens.
cues.zh: 但這是很概括的說明。

cues.en: We look at the frequencies, certain mathematical operations this is the key point: that we're not doing any neural computations.
cues.zh: 看頻率、做數學運算；關鍵是沒有神經運算。

cues.en: We're not creating any neural networks, we're just doing mathematical calculations around the frequencies that we can observe, comparing them to the mathematical calculations we have in our library
cues.zh: 不建立神經網路，只對觀察到的頻率進行數學計算，與預先分析頻率資料庫的計算

cues.en: of pre-analyzed frequencies.
cues.zh: 結果比較。

cues.en: And then we are matching it up.
cues.zh: 再配對。

cues.en: We're finding what word a person is saying, what question they're asking or what the sentence is meaning.
cues.zh: 找出對方說哪個字、問什麼問題，或句子意思。

cues.en: And then that is how we recognize speech.
cues.zh: 這樣辨識語音。

cues.en: So there's another version of natural language processing which is in the green area.
cues.zh: 這是綠色區域的另一種 NLP。

cues.en: Next one is the bag of words model which is used for classification.
cues.zh: 下一個詞袋模型，用於分類。

cues.en: A very, very popular approach for text analysis or natural language processing.
cues.zh: 文字分析或 NLP 非常受歡迎的方法。

cues.en: And what it does is basically, well it also sits in the NLP part, in just the green area, although, as we'll see further on, it can sit both
cues.zh: 同樣位於綠色 NLP 區，不過稍後會看到，可以同時位於

cues.en: in the green area and in the purple area over here.
cues.zh: 綠色與紫色區域。

cues.en: But that's something for a later discussion.
cues.zh: 之後再談。

cues.en: What's the bag of words model does is- there's our bag of words, and the way it works is, you might have like lots of text, for instance here we've got
cues.zh: 詞袋模型怎麼做？這是詞袋；你可能有大量文字，例如這裡有

cues.en: tutors or lecturers or examiners who marked grades
cues.zh: 導師、講師或評分者給分，

cues.en: so who gave a pass or a fail grade to different papers or different assignments that were submitted.
cues.zh: 對提交的報告或作業給及格、不及格。

cues.en: And then they also left a comment.
cues.zh: 並留下評語。

cues.en: So somebody said, "Great job" and left a comment of one meaning a pass.
cues.zh: 有人寫「做得好」，給 1，代表及格。

cues.en: Somebody said, "Amazing work," left a comment of one, "Well done," one, "Very well written," one, and then "Poor effort," zero, "Could have done better," zero "Try harder next time," zero, and so on.
cues.zh: 有人寫「非常棒」，1；「做得好」，1；「寫得很好」，1；「不夠用心」，0；「可以更好」，0；「下次再努力」，0，等等。

cues.en: And so from this, what the bag of words model will do is it will put all these words into a bag and it'll remember.
cues.zh: 詞袋模型會把這些詞放進袋子，記住，

cues.en: So how often does the word grade come up with a one?
cues.zh: great 這個詞與 1 一起出現多少次，

cues.en: And how often does the word grade come up with a zero?
cues.zh: 與 0 一起出現多少次。

cues.en: This is again, a very general explanation, very high level explanation, of what happens.
cues.zh: 這同樣只是很概括、高層次的解釋。

cues.en: But in essence, this is the concept that it'll look at the words and it'll look- it'll try to classify these words,
cues.zh: 但本質是看這些詞，試著分類，

cues.en: it'll try to associate these words with either positive results or a negative result in our case.
cues.zh: 在這個例子裡，把詞與正面或負面結果連結。

cues.en: And so in this case, like amazing would be most likely associated with positive view.
cues.zh: 例如 amazing，很可能與正面看法相關。

cues.en: Don't often see amazing when you're trying to say, when the sentiment is negative, when the person was trying to say something like, the work wasn't well done
cues.zh: 負面情緒、想說作品做得不好時，不常看到 amazing。

cues.en: or well would be associated with one.
cues.zh: well 會與 1 關聯。

cues.en: Like the word work could be associated with both.
cues.zh: work 則可能兩種都有。

cues.en: But then these other words, they would be mostly associated with pass, some like words like poor or harder
cues.zh: 其他這些詞大多和及格有關，poor、harder，

cues.en: or could have maybe would be associated with zeros.
cues.zh: 或 could have，可能與 0 有關。

cues.en: And so then it'll remember that it'll keep these words in a bag and next time something comes up, for instance, somebody says,
cues.zh: 記住並把詞留在袋子，下次有新內容，例如有人說，

cues.en: good, good job, keep, keep it up or something like that.
cues.zh: 「做得好，繼續保持」，之類的。

cues.en: It will analyze the words that are in that new sentence by pulling them out of the bag and looking at them and understanding are they mostly associated ones or zeros?
cues.zh: 會分析新句子的詞，從袋子取出查看，了解大多與 1 還是 0 關聯。

cues.en: And then it'll be able to predict, it'll be able to classify the new comment, even without knowing what the mark was, pass or fail, it will be able to say, based on the comment
cues.zh: 即使不知道成績及格或不及格，也能預測、分類新評語，根據評語，

cues.en: it'll be able to say, Is it a pass or a fail?
cues.zh: 判斷是及格還是不及格。

cues.en: So that's like a very simplistic application of the back of words model.
cues.zh: 這是詞袋模型很簡單的應用。

cues.en: But there's another one, an NLP model.
cues.zh: 又是另一種 NLP 模型。

cues.en: Okay, so let's look at a deep natural language processing model.
cues.zh: 再看深度 NLP 模型。

cues.en: And this one is going to be located over here.
cues.zh: 位於這裡。

cues.en: It's called convolutional neural networks for text recognition.
cues.zh: 叫用於文字辨識的卷積神經網路。

cues.en: So they like the model we're going to be looking at further down is indeed a deep natural language process model.
cues.zh: 稍後要看的模型確實也是深度 NLP，

cues.en: But I was, I I wanted to give an example of a different model.
cues.zh: 但想提供另一個不同模型的例子。

cues.en: So not just the one that we look at but like also a deep natural language process model but a different one.
cues.zh: 不只我們要看的那個，同樣深度 NLP，但不同。

cues.en: And one I came across is when we use convolutional neural networks or text recognition and then further for classification.
cues.zh: 我遇過一種，是用卷積神經網路做文字辨識，再做分類。

cues.en: And so if you're familiar with convolutional networks, or even if you're not, what they're used for is, it's a neural network that is used for mostly image recognition
cues.zh: 如果熟悉 CNN，或即使不熟，它是主要用於影像辨識的神經網路，

cues.en: for like videos, self-driving cars use them to detect obstacles on roads, people and so on.
cues.zh: 例如影片，自駕車用來偵測路上障礙物、行人等等。

cues.en: So mostly it's used for image processing or video processing.
cues.zh: 主要用於影像或影片處理。

cues.en: So it was very interesting to see how convolutional neural networks can actually be used for text processing.
cues.zh: 所以看到 CNN 也能處理文字，很有趣。

cues.en: And the way it works is,
cues.zh: 運作方式是，

cues.en: these words are transformed into a matrix and that's done through an operation called embedding of words.
cues.zh: 透過詞嵌入操作，把詞轉成矩陣。

cues.en: And then once they're in a matrix the same principles as convolution- as were applied for images in convolutional neural networks are applied.
cues.zh: 變成矩陣後，就套用 CNN 處理影像時相同的原理。

cues.en: So there's a convolution operation going through these images.
cues.zh: 對這些影像做卷積運算。

cues.en: Then they're pooled, max pooled or min pooled or sum pooled, and then they're flattened.
cues.zh: 再做池化，最大、最小或總和池化，然後攤平。

cues.en: And then you know, then we have the prediction.
cues.zh: 接著產生預測。

cues.en: So we won't go into detail right now of how convolutional operations work.
cues.zh: 現在不深入卷積運作細節。

cues.en: There's lots of tutorials out there and so on.
cues.zh: 外面有很多教學。

cues.en: And it's just not in the scope of this course because in this course we'll be looking at mostly recurrent neural networks, which is r and n, a different type of neural networks.
cues.zh: 也不在本課範圍，因為本課主要看循環神經網路 RNN，另一種神經網路。

cues.en: But I just wanted to put it out there that you could technically use convolutional neural networks for text recognition, just as you would do with images.
cues.zh: 只是想說，技術上可用 CNN 辨識文字，就像影像一樣。

cues.en: And very interesting concept.
cues.zh: 概念非常有意思。

cues.en: That was one of the earlier ones that was explored.
cues.zh: 這是比較早被探索的方法之一。

cues.en: And then we moved on to recurrent neural networks as we'll see down the track.
cues.zh: 之後走向 RNN，稍後會看到。

cues.en: So there we go, that's another one.
cues.zh: 這就是另一個。

cues.en: And then finally the main model that we'll be looking for, working with, sequence-to-sequence has many, many, many different applications as we'll see further down.
cues.zh: 最後主要要用的序列到序列，有非常多應用，之後會看。

cues.en: And that's the one that's over there.
cues.zh: 位於那裡。

cues.en: So I'll give you a short preview of what's coming up.
cues.zh: 先簡短預告。

cues.en: Looks something like this.
cues.zh: 看起來像這樣。

cues.en: And don't worry, it might look very complex right now, but in a couple of tutorials from here will be very, very comfortable with what's going on here
cues.zh: 別擔心，現在可能很複雜，但幾堂之後，就會很熟悉這裡的情況，

cues.en: and how this whole construct is working and why it's called sequence-to-sequence and what exactly it allows us to do.
cues.zh: 整個結構怎麼運作、為何叫序列到序列，以及能做什麼。

cues.en: So there we go.
cues.zh: 就是這樣。

cues.en: I hope you enjoy this quick overview and comparison of the different types of models and different applications that they have.
cues.zh: 希望你喜歡不同模型類型與應用的快速概覽、比較。

cues.en: And we'll continue next time.
cues.zh: 下次繼續。

cues.en: I look forward to seeing you there.
cues.zh: 期待再見。

cues.en: And until then, enjoy deep nlp.
cues.zh: 在那之前，祝你享受深度 NLP 的樂趣。
